digest:
The day’s work continues to weave together holographic geometry, celestial symmetry, and algebraic structures.  In AdS$_3$ the new PEE‑thread constructions—both for BTZ black branes and finite‑cutoff geometries—show how entanglement currents can be sourced from bulk surfaces and asymptotic boundaries, revealing that coarse‑grained bit‑thread flows need not follow geodesics yet still saturate the RT bottleneck.  A complementary study extends holographic entropy inequalities beyond strong subadditivity, uncovering higher‑order multipartite constraints that sharpen our understanding of RG flows in semiclassical duals.  On the supersymmetric side, freshly identified five‑dimensional saddles uplift to AdS$_3	imes S^3	imes$K3 and reproduce the Farey‑tail expansion of the D1–D5 elliptic genus, while a careful analysis shows that certain black‑ring and lens geometries do not contribute to the index.

Celestial amplitudes receive a boost from two interlocking threads: a light‑ray action for the $mathcal{L}_Lambda w_{1+infty}$ algebra in free CFT$_3$ and its extension to the critical $O(N)$ model, together with a single‑minus graviton computation that maps the amplitude to a BPS index obeying a tower of $w_{1+infty}$ soft theorems.  These results dovetail with the algebraic‑geometry side, where quasimaps to Nakajima quiver varieties are recast as critical loci, and Vafa–Witten invariants on Hirzebruch surfaces are expressed as indefinite theta series—both pointing to deeper modular and Langlands‑type structures.  The topological‑string blowup equations for local Hirzebruch threefolds and the equivariant localization of $N=2$ theories on $mathbb{CP}^2$ further reinforce the emerging bridge between gauge‑theoretic partition functions, modular forms, and representation theory.  Together, these papers highlight a growing synergy between holographic entanglement, celestial symmetry algebras, and algebraic‑geometric methods that promise new insights into higher‑point correlators and the mathematical underpinnings of quantum gravity.

papers.title: Massive Ghost Confinement, Dipole Equation and Multipole States in Quadratic Gravity
papers.authors: Ichiro Oda
papers.abstract: We investigate the problem of confinement of massive ghost, which violates the unitarity of the physical S-matrix, in quadratic gravity on the basis of a manifestly covariant and local canonical operator formalism. First, we reconsider the manifestly covariant quantization of quadratic gravity in the de Donder gauge (the harmonic gauge) from the viewpoint of dipole fields. Next, we also reconsider a possible mechanism of confinement of the massive ghost and derive an effective Lagrangian for asymptotic fields of a BRST quartet where the asymptotic field corresponding to the massive ghost is found to obey a dipole field equation as in the Froissart model, which is a characteristic feature in our formalism. To understand quantum aspects of our theory, we perform a manifestly covariant quantization of the effective Lagrangian in two different ways based on the three-dimensional Fourier transform and the four-dimensional Fourier transform, and derive the same result that the quantum Fock space is spanned by multipole states.
papers.summary: This paper studies confinement of the massive ghost in quadratic gravity using a covariant canonical operator formalism, deriving an effective Lagrangian for a BRST quartet where the ghost obeys a dipole equation. The authors quantize the effective theory in both 3D and 4D Fourier space, showing that the Fock space is spanned by multipole states.

papers.title: Notes on Gepner Construction
papers.authors: Kanade Nishikawa, Taizan Watari
papers.abstract: In this note, we describe the Gepner construction purely as orbifold (rather than a beta-prescription or orbifold-like process). This is done by distinguishing orbifolding by a chiral symmetry from that by a left-right diagonal symmetry, and also by exploiting an extra degree of freedom available in orbifolds of Type 0 SCFTs. We also describe by using the Arf theory how the extra freedom in Type 0 SCFT orbifolds in general (not just in the Gepner construction) should be implemented in higher genus amplitudes. This note also determines when a combinatorial data set of a Gepner construction has a mirror Gepner construction, and also provides two thinking frameworks to determine the SCFT vertex operators of the Gepner model SCFTs with phase ambiguity and branch cuts under control.
papers.summary: This paper reformulates the Gepner construction as an orbifold of Type 0 SCFTs, clarifying the distinction between chiral and diagonal orbifolds and exploiting an extra degree of freedom via Arf theory for higher‑genus amplitudes. It also establishes criteria for mirror Gepner models and provides a framework to control phase ambiguities and branch cuts in the SCFT vertex operators.

papers.title: Quasimaps to Nakajima varieties as critical loci
papers.authors: Spencer Tamagni
papers.abstract: $X$ is a Nakajima quiver variety. In this note we report the observation that the space parameterizing quasimaps from $\mathbb{P}^1$ to $X$, sending infinity to a given point, may be presented globally as the critical locus of an explicit function.
papers.summary: This paper shows that the moduli space of quasimaps from the projective line to a Nakajima quiver variety, with a fixed point at infinity, can be described as the critical locus of an explicit function. This gives a concrete geometric description that may be useful for studying gauge‑theoretic moduli spaces and their connections to representation theory.

papers.title: Vacuum energy problem in anti-de Sitter space
papers.authors: E. V. Arbuzova, A. D. Dolgov
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmological evolution of a universe with an initially large negative vacuum energy, corresponding to an anti-de Sitter (AdS) space-time. Such a universe inevitably contracts and collapses into a singularity. To prevent this collapse, we propose a dynamical mechanism of vacuum energy compensation based on a scalar field non-minimally coupled to the curvature scalar. Numerical and analytical calculations demonstrate that the suggested mechanism completely compensates the gravitational impact of the vacuum energy, successfully driving the curvature to zero. As a result, the universe avoids the singularity and evolves into a power-law expansion, typical for a radiation-dominated cosmology.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a dynamical scalar field mechanism that cancels a large negative vacuum energy in an AdS universe, preventing collapse and driving the curvature to zero. This leads to a nonsingular cosmology that asymptotically approaches a radiation-dominated power-law expansion.

papers.title: Robust Finite-Momentum Instabilities in Dense Matter
papers.authors: André G. da Silva, Ricardo L. S. Farias, Theo Motta, William R. Tavares
papers.abstract: The predicted extent of inhomogeneous chiral phases in effective models of quantum chromodynamics is notoriously sensitive to ultraviolet regularization. We show that this sensitivity is largely artificial. In the two-flavor Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model, conventional implementations of three-dimensional cutoff, Pauli--Villars, and proper-time regularization produce strongly different finite-momentum instability regions. Once ultraviolet regulators are restricted to genuinely divergent vacuum contributions, however, all three prescriptions yield nearly identical stability diagrams. Both the onset of the moat regime and the subsequent finite-momentum instability become quantitatively robust. The apparent scheme dependence originates from regulating ultraviolet-finite medium contributions associated with the Fermi-surface response. Our results identify spatially modulated chiral correlations as a genuine property of the dense medium rather than an artifact of the ultraviolet prescription.
papers.summary: This paper demonstrates that finite-momentum instabilities in the two-flavor NJL model are robust against different ultraviolet regularization schemes once only divergent vacuum contributions are regulated, revealing spatially modulated chiral correlations as a genuine feature of dense QCD matter. It clarifies that scheme dependence originates from regulating finite medium contributions tied to the Fermi surface, resolving a long-standing ambiguity in effective model predictions of inhomogeneous chiral phases.

papers.title: Imaginary Rotation Breaks Charge Conjugation in Hot QCD
papers.authors: Rin Takada
papers.abstract: Starting from the identity $\mathrm{e}^{2π\mathrm{i}J_z}=(-1)^{F}=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}πQ}$ for the angular momentum, fermion parity, and quark number operators, valid on the color-singlet physical state space, we derive a density-operator identity that ties imaginary rotation to an imaginary quark chemical potential, $ρ(Ω_I/T+2π,θ_q)=ρ(Ω_I/T,θ_q+π)$. It follows that the imaginarily rotating system of $SU(3)$ QCD at $(Ω_I/T,θ_q)=(2π,0)$ is mapped exactly onto the Roberge-Weiss point $(0,π)$, where charge conjugation is spontaneously broken above the Roberge-Weiss endpoint. This conclusion depends on no model and no approximation. Minimizing the one-loop effective potential on the rotation axis over the entire $SU(3)$ Weyl alcove, we further obtain analytically, for three massless quark flavors, the second-order transition point $Ω_{I,C}/(πT)=(22-2\sqrt{22})/9$ at which $\mathrm{Im}\,L$ rises continuously, and the first-order transition point $Ω_{I,\mathrm{lock}}/(πT)=2/3+2\sqrt{111}/27$ at which the minimum locks into the nontrivial center elements. In the massless one-loop approximation a continuous degeneracy appears in full QCD and in pure Yang-Mills theory alike, but on the full-QCD side it is merely accidental, lifted by a finite strange-quark mass. Finally, we state the conditions under which the exact relations and the on-axis predictions can be tested in lattice QCD.
papers.summary: The paper shows that an imaginary rotation in SU(3) QCD is equivalent to an imaginary quark chemical potential, mapping the system at (Ω_I/T,θ_q)=(2π,0) onto the Roberge–Weiss point where charge conjugation is spontaneously broken. Using a one‑loop effective potential it analytically locates the second‑order and first‑order transition points along the rotation axis for three massless flavors and discusses how a finite strange‑quark mass lifts a degeneracy.

papers.title: PEE threads and bit threads in gravitational subregions of AdS
papers.authors: Debarshi Basu, Qiang Wen
papers.abstract: Motivated by the kinematic-space description of gravitational subregions \cite{Basu:2026hbg}, we allow partial entanglement entropy (PEE) threads to be sourced not only from the asymptotic boundary, but also from boundaries of subregions. Based on this setup, we develop a framework to construct configurations for PEE threads and bit threads sourced from surfaces in the AdS bulk. The situations we have analyzed include the Poincaré AdS$_3$ and the planar BTZ black brane with an end-of-the-world (EOW) brane, and the entanglement wedges of boundary multi-intervals. We construct novel configurations of PEE threads and bit threads in these situations, which shed new light in our understanding of the AdS$_3$/BCFT$_2$ correspondence and the holography defined in the entanglement wedge motivated by surface/state correspondence. A notable feature we found is that, although the elementary PEE threads are geodesics, the integral curves of the coarse-grained bit-thread current are generically not geodesics. Across the explicit constructions, the integrated source currents reduce to endpoint distance-difference potentials, which make divergencelessness, the norm bound and bottleneck saturation geometrically transparent. Our results clarify how boundary, brane, horizon and RT-surface degrees of freedom participate in holographic entanglement and provide a concrete link between PEE, bit threads, subregion kinematic space and the surface/state correspondence.
papers.summary: The paper develops a framework for constructing partial entanglement entropy (PEE) threads and bit threads sourced from both asymptotic boundaries and bulk surfaces in AdS$_3$, providing explicit configurations in Poincaré AdS, BTZ black branes with EOW branes, and multi-interval entanglement wedges. It reveals that while elementary PEE threads follow geodesics, the coarse-grained bit‑thread currents generally do not, offering new geometric insights into holographic entanglement, AdS$_3$/BCFT$_2$, and the surface/state correspondence.

papers.title: PEE threads and bit-threads in BTZ black brane and finite-cutoff AdS$_3$
papers.authors: Debarshi Basu, Ashish Chandra, Qiang Wen
papers.abstract: We develop PEE thread flows for the planar BTZ black brane and finite-cutoff holography. Exact geodesic-distance kernels define source-resolved PEE thread currents whose superposition gives divergenceless bit-thread fields. In BTZ, boundary-boundary and boundary-horizon sectors reproduce the entanglement contour and thermal horizon flux. At finite cutoff, the two-point PEE kernels are smooth and select macroscopic flows that are generically non-geodesic despite being built from geodesic elementary threads. We compare these PEE-selected flows with independent normal-geodesic bit-thread flows and show that they saturate the same RT bottleneck while differing in boundary calibration, endpoint pairing and off-bottleneck structure. The resulting constructions make explicit both the endpoint organization of finite-cutoff entanglement and the nonuniqueness of holographic max flows.
papers.summary: The paper constructs PEE thread flows for the planar BTZ black brane and finite-cutoff AdS$_3$, deriving exact geodesic-distance kernels that generate source-resolved PEE thread currents and their superposition into divergenceless bit-thread fields. It compares these PEE-selected flows to normal-geodesic bit-thread flows, showing they saturate the same RT bottleneck while differing in boundary calibration and off-bottleneck structure, thereby illuminating the nonuniqueness of holographic max flows.

papers.title: Reconstructing $f(R)$ gravity from generalized entropies: exact Lagrangians
papers.authors: Ankit Anand, Sahil Devdutt, Kimet Jusufi, Ayan Chatterjee, Emmanuel N. Saridakis
papers.abstract: Generalized horizon entropies are widely used as theoretical modifications of the Bekenstein-Hawking area law, but through the Wald construction they may also encode modifications of the underlying gravitational dynamics. We reconstruct metric $f(R)$ gravity from prescribed entropy-area relations and show that the procedure is intrinsically branch dependent through the required area-curvature map. On the maximally symmetric branch, where $A=48π/R$ exactly, the reconstruction reduces to a single quadrature and can be performed non-perturbatively. We obtain closed-form Lagrangians for several generalized entropies and show that an entropy term $a~S_{BH}^{q}$ generates a curvature term proportional to $R^{2-q}$. In particular, Kaniadakis entropy produces a $1/R$ correction, while logarithmic entropy generates an $R^2\ln R$ term. We further derive a branch-independent criterion, $\partial_{R}^{2} f=(ds/dR)d(S/s)/ds$, relating Dolgov-Kawasaki stability directly to the entropy functional, together with $m_{\rm sc}^2=S'(s)/(3f_{RR})$ on the maximally symmetric branch. Comparison with the fixed-mass Schwarzschild-de Sitter branch reveals different reconstructed Lagrangians and reversed stability properties. Finally, the weak-isolated-horizon boost charge reproduces the original generalized entropy. These results establish a direct non-perturbative link between generalized horizon thermodynamics and modified gravitational dynamics.
papers.summary: The authors demonstrate that generalized horizon entropies can be used to reconstruct metric f(R) gravity, deriving explicit Lagrangians for several entropy forms and establishing a branch‑dependent area–curvature mapping. They also provide a stability criterion linking Dolgov–Kawasaki stability to the entropy functional and show that different branches yield distinct Lagrangians with reversed stability properties.

papers.title: Odderon in the diffractive dip region
papers.authors: E. G. S. Luna, M. G. Ryskin, V. A. Khoze
papers.abstract: We examine possible $C$-odd effects in elastic proton-proton and proton-antiproton scattering in the diffractive dip region. Collider data with $\sqrt{s}>500$ GeV are fitted for $0.2<|t|<1~\GeV^2$, using a simple Regge-inspired parametrization of effective $C$-even and $C$-odd amplitudes. The relative phases are not left free, but are fixed by the signature factors of the corresponding even and odd contributions. In this way, the real and imaginary parts of each term are linked by crossing. The $C$-even amplitude is first described by three effective Pomeron-like terms. The $C$-odd sector is then tested with several one-term Odderon-like forms. We find that the fits do not require a stable nonzero $C$-odd term: the odd contribution is either compatible with zero or becomes weakly constrained when we allow extra freedom. We then test whether the conclusion is changed by adding either a fourth Pomeron-like term or a second Odderon-like term. The improvement obtained with the fourth Pomeron-like term is mainly $C$-even, while the second Odderon-like term is not resolved as an independent contribution. These results provide a complementary test of recent determinations of the Odderon amplitude based on scaling and analyticity.
papers.summary: The authors fit elastic pp and p\bar{p} scattering data in the diffractive dip region using a Regge-inspired model with C-even and C-odd amplitudes, finding no compelling evidence for a stable Odderon contribution. Adding extra Pomeron or Odderon terms does not significantly alter the conclusion, providing a complementary test of recent Odderon determinations.

papers.title: Rare Exclusive Top Decays t , b M and Vector-Meson Helicity
papers.authors: M. Ahmadi, M. Monemzadeh, N. Tazimi
papers.abstract: We present a leading-order study of the rare exclusive decays $t \to bM$, where $M$ denotes a pseudoscalar or vector meson. Starting from the tree-level transition $t \to bW^* \to b(q\bar q')$ and using a factorization approximation, we derive compact expressions for the amplitudes and partial widths in which the long-distance QCD dynamics is encoded in the meson decay constants $f_M$. We provide numerical branching-ratio predictions for representative modes such as $t \to bπ^+$, $t \to bK^+$, $t \to bD_s^{(*)}$, and $t \to bB_c^{(*)}$, finding $\mathrm{Br} \sim 10^{-8}$--$10^{-7}$. For vector final states, we derive helicity amplitudes and Standard-Model polarization fractions, and we outline the sensitivity of these observables to anomalous chiral $tWb$ couplings in the limit $m_b \to 0$. Our results provide an updated Standard Model (SM) baseline for rare exclusive top-quark decays and a starting point for EFT interpretations of non-standard charged-current interactions.
papers.summary: This paper studies rare exclusive top-quark decays into a bottom quark and a light meson, deriving leading-order amplitudes using factorization and meson decay constants. It provides branching ratio predictions and helicity analyses, offering a Standard-Model baseline for future EFT studies of charged-current interactions.

papers.title: Decoupling saddles of the gravitational index and the Farey tail
papers.authors: Davide Cassani, Alejandro Ruipérez, Enrico Turetta
papers.abstract: We first construct general saddles of the five-dimensional gravitational supersymmetric index with $S^1\times\mathbb{R}^4$ asymptotics, carrying an arbitrary number of electric charges and Gibbons-Hawking centers. We then uplift the three-charge configurations to type IIB supergravity, obtaining solutions asymptotic to $S^1\times \mathbb{R}^4\times S^1\times {\rm K}3$, carrying D1-D5-P charges. Upon taking a decoupling limit, these solutions yield asymptotically Euclidean AdS$_3\times S^3\times {\rm K}3$ candidate saddles of the dual CFT$_2$ elliptic genus. We focus on the two-center saddles, which involve three integers specifying an orbifold action. Depending on these integers, the saddles may or may not possess a Euclidean horizon, and may be smooth or exhibit orbifold singularities. We give the on-shell action of these two-center saddles in the appropriate ensemble and establish a precise match with the Farey-tail expansion of the elliptic genus. The horizonless saddles are the Euclidean version of fractional spectral-flow solutions previously discussed in the literature, corresponding to $({\rm AdS}_3\times S^3)/\mathbb{Z}_k$ orbifolds. The black hole saddles are modular images of the horizonless ones. They generalize the well-known ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ family of BTZ black holes by placing it in the background of the $\mathbb{Z}_k$ orbifold. We also consider the asymptotically AdS$_3\times S^3$ solutions arising as decoupling limit of five-dimensional black ring and black lens saddles, provide their on-shell action and confirm that they do not contribute to the D1-D5 elliptic genus.
papers.summary: The paper constructs new supersymmetric saddles in five‑dimensional gravity that uplift to type IIB solutions asymptotic to AdS$_3	imes S^3	imes$K3, matching the Farey‑tail expansion of the D1‑D5 elliptic genus and revealing a rich structure of horizonless orbifold geometries and their black‑hole modular images. It clarifies how these geometries encode microstate contributions to the elliptic genus and demonstrates that certain AdS$_3	imes S^3$ saddles from black rings and lenses do not contribute to the index.

papers.title: Stationary Dirac condensates around Kerr black holes
papers.authors: Sen Guo, Peng-Yu Chen, Yi-Han Huang, Xin Li, Yu Liang, Kai Lin, Lin Wen
papers.abstract: Ultralight bosonic fields can form macroscopic clouds around rotating black holes, whereas the existence of analogous stationary fermionic condensates is strictly constrained by their intrinsic spin. Here we establish a complete geometric and kinematic framework to resolve the stationary bound states of massive Dirac fields on Kerr and Kerr-Newman backgrounds. By mapping the Kerr-Dirac system to a globally integrated sourced radial problem, we strictly isolate the boundary constraints dictated by horizon causality. The angular sector reveals a fundamental topological distinction: because the azimuthal quantum number is strictly half-integer, the regular boundary branches prevent the local field density from vanishing on the rotation axis. Consequently, rotating fermionic clouds inherently form globally filled, oblate geometries, in stark contrast to the hollow toroidal structures characteristic of scalar condensates. Crucially, our radial indicial analysis unveils the exact mathematical origin of the absence of synchronized Dirac hair. Precisely at the kinematic synchronization locus, the Frobenius matrix of the Dirac operator is non-defective and entirely devoid of logarithmic divergences. Without these singular branches to be selectively excised by boundary regularity, the physical burden of existence falls entirely onto the causal flux barrier, which strictly trivializes the zero-source amplitude. This synchronization veto demonstrates that a black hole's capacity to support macroscopic stationary fields is governed not merely by superradiant kinematics, but by the profound interplay between local horizon causality and quantum spin statistics.
papers.summary: The authors construct a complete framework for stationary bound states of massive Dirac fields on Kerr and Kerr–Newman spacetimes, showing that fermionic clouds cannot synchronize with the horizon and thus cannot form macroscopic hair. They demonstrate that the absence of synchronized Dirac hair arises from horizon causality and the half‑integer azimuthal quantum number, leading to globally filled oblate geometries rather than hollow toroidal scalar condensates.

papers.title: Topological String Blowup Equations via Stable Pairs
papers.authors: Lutian Zhao
papers.abstract: For the local Hirzebruch threefolds \(Y_\ell=\operatorname{Tot}_{\mathbb F_\ell}K_{\mathbb F_\ell}\), \(0\leq\ell\leq2\), we prove blowup equations for the two-variable, torus-equivariant symmetrized \(K\)-theoretic stable-pair series. After division by the fibre-class contribution, four-chart localization is identified coefficientwise with the equivariant Euler-characteristic series of \((\det\mathcal V)^\ell\) on moduli spaces of framed rank-two sheaves, with \(\mathcal V\) tautological. The framed-sheaf blowup formulas then give the unity and vanishing equations; for \(\ell=2\) this is an identity of localized indices. We state separately the two conjectures needed for the conditional local \(\mathbb P^2\) equations, the general Huang--Sun--Wang conjecture, and a rational-elliptic specialization involving the \(E_8\) lattice.
papers.summary: The paper establishes blowup equations for the K‑theoretic stable‑pair invariants of local Hirzebruch threefolds, relating them to equivariant Euler characteristics on moduli of framed rank‑two sheaves. These results provide new algebraic tools that could feed into topological string computations and, indirectly, into gauge/string dualities.

papers.title: Beyond Strong Subadditivity: Holographic Entropy Inequalities Along Renormalization Group Flows
papers.authors: Ning Bao, Christian Ferko
papers.abstract: Strong subadditivity (SSA) on a common light cone gives the Casini-Huerta entropic proof of the three-dimensional $F$-theorem. We ask whether holographic entropy inequalities beyond SSA similarly constrain renormalization group flows for which every intermediate theory admits a semiclassical holographic description. For small, disjoint deformations of a common light-cone region, we show that the second-order response of a broad class of balanced holographic inequalities depends only on pairwise correlations already controlled by SSA. A six-party example shows that the full finite inequality nevertheless contains genuinely multipartite information, so its disappearance is a limitation of the second-order expansion rather than of the inequality itself. Two natural finite constructions do not recover the missing information. We nevertheless find two ways in which information beyond SSA survives. A five-party inequality bounds the rate at which a conditional correlation grows as one region is enlarged. Separately, a continuum limit of the odd-cyclic inequalities gives a constraint on the angular shape dependence of entanglement entropy, and Lorentz symmetry relates this constraint to radial evolution. Thus holographic entropy inequalities beyond SSA do constrain entanglement along RG flows, although we do not obtain a second universal analogue of the $F$-function.
papers.summary: This paper extends holographic entropy inequalities beyond strong subadditivity to constrain renormalization group flows in theories with semiclassical holographic duals. It demonstrates that while second‑order responses are governed by pairwise correlations, higher‑order multipartite information survives and yields new constraints on conditional correlations and angular shape dependence of entanglement entropy.

papers.title: Single-Minus Graviton Amplitudes from Matrix Theory
papers.authors: Alfredo Guevara, Alexandru Lupsasca, Juan Maldacena, Andrew Strominger
papers.abstract: The $n$-point single-minus graviton amplitudes are nonzero in a special kinematic region that preserves some supersymmetry when embedded in supergravity. We compute these amplitudes within the BFSS matrix theory by relating them to an index problem considered by A. Sen. More precisely, the single-minus amplitudes are obtained from an index that counts BPS states in the Coulomb branch of four-dimensional ${\cal N}=4$ super Yang-Mills. We explicitly check this relation in a specific kinematic region by computing the index using BPS wall-crossing formulae and matching it to the gravity result. We further employ BPS wall-crossing to show that the index satisfies a tower of $w_{1+\infty}$ soft theorems in any kinematic regime, again matching gravity. Finally, we show that for certain kinematics, the single-minus amplitudes can be realized by scattering a graviton off a plane wave.
papers.summary: The authors compute n‑point single‑minus graviton amplitudes in a supersymmetric kinematic regime by mapping them to a BPS index in the Coulomb branch of 4d N=4 SYM, and verify the result using wall‑crossing techniques. They further show that the index obeys a tower of w_{1+∞} soft theorems and can be realized as graviton scattering off a plane wave in special kinematics.

papers.title: Chaos in Yang-Mills
papers.authors: Barel Skuratovsky
papers.abstract: We study the dynamics of pure-gauge SU(N) through the time evolution of a spatial Wilson loop. We compute its out-of-time-order correlator at weak 't Hooft coupling and large N, and propose a framework for the strong-coupling description. We find that operators in pure-gauge Yang-Mills grow only when the group is non-abelian and d>2, and conjecture that pure gauge theories are chaotic only when non-abelian at d>2. Even at weak coupling the correlator's exponent inherits the IR sensitivity of the gluon self-energy imaginary part, which rests on the non-perturbative magnetic scale. We then explore the possibility that the loop's own size supplies that scale, since the loop operator is blind to any momenta softer than 1/2R. With the cutoff imposed that way the exponent changes sign at a critical diameter: smaller loops scramble, larger ones do not, and the scrambling time diverges at the crossing. The transition follows from that cutoff. Further investigation, in particular a first-principles treatment of the thermal decay width, is required to establish whether it is physical.
papers.summary: The authors compute the out‑of‑time‑order correlator of a spatial Wilson loop in pure SU(N) Yang–Mills at weak coupling and large N, finding that chaos only appears for non‑abelian groups in dimensions greater than two and that the Lyapunov exponent is controlled by the non‑perturbative magnetic scale. They propose that the loop size itself can act as an IR cutoff, leading to a size‑dependent transition between scrambling and non‑scrambling regimes that warrants further first‑principles investigation.

papers.title: Exact All-Level Positivity of the Bosonic Veneziano Amplitude
papers.authors: Qi Chen, Yuan Yin
papers.abstract: Tree-level partial-wave unitarity of the open bosonic Veneziano amplitude follows indirectly from the no-ghost theorem, but a direct proof from the beta function has been missing at the critical dimension. We prove nonnegativity at every mass level and spin throughout the sharp range 3 < D <= 26, using a Bessel recurrence that reduces the infinite sign problem to a manifestly positive bulk and a finite exact boundary.
papers.summary: The authors provide a direct proof of the nonnegativity of the open bosonic Veneziano amplitude at all mass levels and spins for dimensions 3<D<=26, using a Bessel recurrence that isolates a manifestly positive bulk and a finite exact boundary. This resolves a long-standing gap in the direct beta‑function proof of tree‑level partial‑wave unitarity in the critical dimension.

papers.title: 21-cm Brightness Temperature in a Unified-Dark-Sector Horndeski Theory
papers.authors: Bertha Cuadros-Melgar, Thanasis Karakasis, Eleftherios Papantonopoulos, Maria Petronikolou
papers.abstract: We investigate the impact of scalar-tensor theories on the 21cm brightness temperature. We consider a specific model in Horndeski scalar-tensor theory in which dark matter and dark energy in the framework of shift-symmetric generalized Galileon theories was described and an effective unified cosmic fluid was obtained. We calculate the Hubble parameter of the model and we plot the curve of the evolution of the 21-cm temperature in a specific range of the redshift parameter $z$ and compare it to the curve corresponding to $Λ$CDM paradigm.
papers.summary: This paper studies the effect of a shift-symmetric Horndeski scalar-tensor model on the 21‑cm brightness temperature, deriving the Hubble parameter and comparing the predicted temperature evolution to ΛCDM. It focuses on cosmological observables rather than high-energy or mathematical structures.

papers.title: Anomalous behavior of Wilson fermions in the presence of monopoles
papers.authors: Manuel Cortina, Rajamani Narayanan, Ray Romero
papers.abstract: Three dimensional compact U(1) gauge theory supports a finite density of monopoles at a fixed lattice gauge coupling. After showing evidence for the expected dependence on the lattice coupling of the density of monopoles, we study the low lying spectrum of a two flavors of two-component Wilson fermions as a function of the bare Wilson mass. The Wilson-Dirac operator that realizes the two flavors are hermitian conjugate of each other to restore parity invariance and the commutativity of the two operators expected in the typical continuum limit is not the case in the presence of monopoles for all values of the lattice gauge coupling. This results in an anomalous behavior where we see clear evidence for the presence of very small eigenvalues for a wide range of a particular sign of the bare Wilson mass. These eigenmodes are typically in one-to-one correspondence with the number of monopoles as defined by the gauge field and the spectrum associated with these modes are separated by a gap from the bulk in the asymptotic regime of the lattice gauge coupling. The eigenvalues come in pairs around zero and the eigenvalues of one sign couple to the monopoles while the modes of the opposite sign couple to the anti-monopole implying flavor symmetry breaking.
papers.summary: The study examines how monopole density in 3D compact U(1) gauge theory affects the low‑lying spectrum of two‑flavor Wilson fermions, revealing anomalously small eigenvalues tied to monopole number and indicating flavor symmetry breaking. These effects persist across lattice couplings and are linked to the non‑commutativity of hermitian conjugate Wilson‑Dirac operators in the presence of monopoles.

papers.title: Convergence of the conformal Ward identity in the derivative expansion approximation
papers.authors: Jorge Ibañez, Matthieu Tissier, Gonzalo De Polsi
papers.abstract: Conformal invariance is expected to be an emergent property of many systems in their critical regime. However, approximation schemes generically spoil this property. This is in particular the case of the derivative expansion, a widely used approximation scheme in the framework of the functional renormalization group. In this article, we consider Ward identities associated with conformal invariance in the 3-d Ising universality class with truncations at order 4 (next-to-next-to-leading order) in the derivative expansion, with $Z_2$ invariant composite operators. Our results confirm that the regulating functions which yield a small breaking of conformal invariance also present a small sensitivity of the universal critical exponents with the choice of this regulating function. We also show that, in the vicinity of regulator-parameter values for which the conformal constraints are best satisfied, the breaking of conformal invariance reduces as the order of the derivative expansion is increased, providing a new indication of the convergence of this approximation scheme.
papers.summary: This work studies the convergence of the conformal Ward identity within the derivative expansion of the functional renormalization group applied to the 3‑dimensional Ising model. The authors find that regulator choices that minimize conformal symmetry breaking also reduce the sensitivity of critical exponents, indicating that higher orders in the derivative expansion bring the approximation closer to exact conformal invariance.

papers.title: Tropical Open Strings in a Kalb-Ramond Background
papers.authors: Sarthak Duary, Vi Hong, Sourav Maji
papers.abstract: We study tropical open strings arising from the analytically continued action of tropological sigma models in the presence of a constant Kalb-Ramond background. We show that the background field separates the theory into a generic sector and a critical sector. In the generic sector, the canonical structure produces a kinematical nonlocal bracket between the transverse and leafwise target-space coordinates. At the critical value of the Kalb-Ramond field, the Legendre map degenerates and the theory develops a primary constraint, requiring quantization by the Dirac-Bergmann procedure. This critical sector has a finite reduced phase-space structure and differs from the naive limit of the generic theory.
papers.summary: This paper investigates tropical open strings in a constant Kalb-Ramond background, showing that the background splits the theory into generic and critical sectors. In the generic sector a nonlocal bracket arises, while at the critical value the Legendre map degenerates, leading to a constrained system that must be quantized via the Dirac-Bergmann procedure.

papers.title: Remarks on Vafa-Witten theory, or how to sit on a wall
papers.authors: Sergei Alexandrov, Aradhita Chattopadhyaya
papers.abstract: We prove three results about refined $SU(N)$ VW invariants on Hirzebruch surfaces. First, we crucially simplify the modular anomaly equation satisfied by the generating series of these invariants by expressing it in terms of complementary generalized error functions, which requires extending these error functions to their singular loci. Second, we evaluate the variation of the modular completions of the generating series upon change of polarization. Finally, a representation of the generating functions in terms of indefinite theta series allows us to compute VW invariants at the walls of marginal stability, and to express them in terms of the invariants on the two sides of the wall and those of lower ranks. All the results exhibit a universal structure suggesting their wider applicability.
papers.summary: This paper refines SU(N) Vafa‑Witten invariants on Hirzebruch surfaces by simplifying the modular anomaly equation using generalized error functions, and shows how the generating series change under polarization shifts. It further expresses the invariants as indefinite theta series, enabling wall‑crossing computations that relate invariants across stability walls and to lower‑rank cases.

papers.title: Slowly Rolling on a Quantum Correction
papers.authors: Ido Ben-Dayan, Ayushi Srivastava, Amresh Verma
papers.abstract: Recent advances in cosmological measurements such as DESI and ACT may indicate an increase in the preferred value of the spectral tilt $n_s$ such that it disfavors rather popular models such as the Higgs or Starobinski inflation models. We argue that it actually means that the data is now sensitive enough to quantum corrections beyond simple tree-level models. Resurrecting the old theme of Coleman-Weinberg effective potential, we analyze the predictions of such models, as well as likelihood analysis, leading to a more established and interesting predictive framework.
papers.summary: The paper investigates how quantum corrections to the inflaton potential, modeled via the Coleman–Weinberg effective potential, can shift the spectral tilt $n_s$ in light of recent DESI and ACT data. It argues that these corrections become phenomenologically relevant, offering a predictive framework beyond simple tree-level inflationary models.

papers.title: Equivariant Localization for N=2 Theories with Hypermultiplets
papers.authors: Matthias Dennemann, Jan Manschot
papers.abstract: Equivariant localization in the $Ω$-background is a powerful technique for the evaluation of the partition function of $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetric field theory on a toric four-manifold. For the complex projective plane $\mathbb{CP}^2$, we apply equivariant localization to supersymmetric Yang-Mills theories with gauge groups $SU(2)$ and $SO(3)$ with $N_f$ massive hypermultiplets in the fundamental representation, and the $\mathcal{N}=2^*$ theory with the hypermultiplet in the adjoint representation. We evaluate equivariant correlation functions, which provide an equivariant extension of intersection numbers of moduli spaces of instantons on $\mathbb{CP}^2$, such as Euler numbers and Segre invariants. In the non-equivariant limit, we compare our results with the evaluation using low energy field theory and integration over the $u$-plane. Using this comparison, we identify a specific overall factor, which captures the difference between a partition function for gauge group $U(2)$ and $SU(2)$ or $SO(3)$ on a compact four-manifold. We also discuss our results in the context of $S$-duality of the $N_f=4$ and $\mathcal{N}=2^*$ theory, which includes the triality automorphism group of the flavor group for $N_f=4$.
papers.summary: This work applies equivariant localization in the Ω‑background to compute partition functions and equivariant correlation functions for N=2 supersymmetric Yang–Mills theories on CP^2, including SU(2), SO(3) and N=2* cases with hypermultiplets. The authors compare the results to low‑energy u‑plane integrals, identify a universal factor distinguishing U(2) from SU(2)/SO(3) partition functions, and discuss implications for S‑duality and flavor triality.

papers.title: Anti-Ultralocality and Plateau Models of Inflation
papers.authors: Joshua Shterenberg, David Garfinkle, Anna I. Rosenzweig, David Shlivko, Paul J. Steinhardt
papers.abstract: Anti-ultralocality refers to the growth of spatial gradient terms relative to velocity terms in the coupled Einstein--scalar field equations. It is a characteristic feature of decelerated expansion before the onset of inflation. Previous numerical relativity studies have shown that anti-ultralocality prevents the onset of inflation in models with power-law inflaton potentials. In this paper, we show that models with plateau-shaped inflaton potentials, which are considered to be the simplest way to generate a tensor-to-scalar ratio below current observational upper limits, are especially vulnerable to anti-ultralocality effects. The reasons are the flatness of the plateau and the energy density gap of $\sim 10$ orders of magnitude between the Planck density and the plateau potential energy. To study the problem, we develop a protocol for assessing the viability of inflationary models in general, and we apply it to a plateau potential using a previously validated numerical relativity code. We find that, starting from generic initial conditions, the growth of gradient terms in the Einstein equations relative to non-gradient terms either prevents inflation from lasting for enough $e$-folds or triggers a phase of quantum runaway. We show that the fine-tuning of initial conditions necessary to avoid these issues becomes more severe as the energy scale of inflation is made smaller, disfavoring common approaches for reducing the tensor-to-scalar ratio.
papers.summary: This paper investigates how anti-ultralocality—where spatial gradients dominate over time derivatives—can thwart inflation in plateau-like scalar potentials, using numerical relativity to show that generic initial conditions either fail to produce sufficient e‑folds or trigger runaway behavior. The authors argue that the fine‑tuning required becomes worse as the inflationary scale is lowered, casting doubt on plateau models as a simple way to suppress the tensor‑to‑scalar ratio.

papers.title: Genus 4 Supermoduli Space Is Not Projected
papers.authors: Ron Donagi, Simone Noja
papers.abstract: The supermoduli stack ${\mathfrak M}_g$, parametrizing smooth unpunctured super Riemann surfaces of genus $g$, is known to be non-projected for $g \ge 5$. We extend this result to the even-spin component of ${\mathfrak M}_4$. This is done by exhibiting an appropriate compact curve in the spin moduli space ${\mathcal S\mathcal M}_4^{+}$, and computing the restriction to it of the class obstructing the projectedness of ${\mathfrak M}_4^{+}$. This restriction turns out to be non-zero, proving that ${\mathfrak M}_4^{+}$ is non-projected.
papers.summary: The paper proves that the even‑spin component of the genus‑4 supermoduli space is non‑projected by constructing a compact curve in the spin moduli space and showing the obstruction class restricts non‑trivially. This result extends the known non‑projectedness for higher genus to genus four, sharpening our understanding of the geometry underlying superstring perturbation theory.

papers.title: Low-Frequency Gravitational Bremsstrahlung and Memory in a Medium
papers.authors: Diego Blas, Silvia Gasparotto, Hitoshi Murayama, Jan Schütte-Engel, Jann Zosso
papers.abstract: Gravitational radiation from the early Universe offers a powerful window into physics beyond the Standard Model (SM). In this paper, we investigate the low-frequency tail of gravitational radiation produced by the decay of massive particles. The energy spectrum in Minkowski space-time, $dE/dω$, exhibits two distinct regimes: a flat bremsstrahlung/memory spectrum above a characteristic cutoff frequency and a suppressed quadratic frequency scaling below it. The typical rate of momentum change of the decay products determines the cutoff frequency. We calculate $dE/dω$ in two independent but equivalent ways: using Weinberg's soft graviton theorem and by solving the equations of motion. This further establishes the connection between Weinberg's soft graviton theorem and the gravitational memory formula, which we generalize to incorporate the effects of final-state scattering. We then compute the cosmological stochastic gravitational energy spectrum $h^2Ω_{\rm h}$ generated by many particle decays in the early Universe. We demonstrate that $h^2Ω_{\rm h}$ exhibits linear scaling with frequency above the cutoff frequency, transitioning to cubic scaling below it. Our findings reveal a suppression of the low-frequency signal compared to a naive linear extrapolation, with implications for detection prospects. Our results also reveal the connection between bremsstrahlung and memory in the context of cosmological stochastic gravitational energy spectra from the early Universe.
papers.summary: This paper computes the low-frequency tail of gravitational radiation from massive particle decays, showing a flat bremsstrahlung/memory spectrum above a cutoff and a quadratic suppression below it. It connects Weinberg's soft graviton theorem to the memory formula, derives the cosmological stochastic energy spectrum, and discusses implications for detection.

papers.title: Emergence of Kastor-Traschen spacetime from a nonlinear Dirac system
papers.authors: Daisuke Ida
papers.abstract: We establish a uniqueness theorem in four-dimensional spacetime, demonstrating that a nonlinear spinor system naturally constrains the background geometry to the Kastor-Traschen spacetime, which describes dynamical, cosmic multi-black-holes. By analyzing a nonlinear field equation where the super-covariant derivative of a Dirac spinor is sourced by intrinsic fermion currents, we evaluate its integrability under two physical requirements: a phase-locking condition enforcing a real hermitian product $\overlineψ_R ψ_L$, and a pure-electric source condition. We show that the field equation uniquely compels the spinor to be an eigenvector of the super-covariant Dirac operator, with the eigenvalue dynamically identified as the Hubble constant of the de Sitter background. These results provide a novel geometric mechanism wherein both the cosmological constant and dynamical black hole configurations spontaneously emerge from fermion condensates.
papers.summary: The authors prove that a nonlinear Dirac system with a phase‑locking and pure‑electric source forces the background geometry to be the Kastor‑Traschen multi‑black‑hole spacetime, with the eigenvalue of the super‑covariant Dirac operator identified as the de Sitter Hubble constant. This establishes a novel mechanism by which both the cosmological constant and dynamical black‑hole configurations arise from fermion condensates.

papers.title: CFT$_3$ Realizations and Celestial Representation Theory of the $\mathcal{L}_Λw_{1+\infty}$ Algebra
papers.authors: Bin Zhu
papers.abstract: We study CFT$_3$ realizations and celestial representations of the $\mathcal{L}_Λw_{1+\infty}$ algebra. Free scalar and Dirac theories yield the same one-particle light-ray action. This action extends to the critical $O(N)$ model at $N=\infty$, while regulated moments reproduce the pairwise algebra in the large-but-finite-$N$ correlators studied here. In the celestial hard-graviton module, the projected null conditions select $Δ=3$ uniquely, and a closed raising subalgebra annihilates $G^+_3$ exactly. The nonzero-$Λ$ quadratic Casimir has eigenvalue three throughout the hard module, and the exact annihilators and low-spin Ward identities give compatible differential-difference equations for celestial correlators.
papers.summary: The authors construct a light‑ray action for the $mathcal{L}_Λw_{1+infty}$ algebra in free scalar and Dirac CFT$_3$ and extend it to the critical $O(N)$ model at large $N$, showing that regulated moments reproduce the pairwise algebra in finite‑$N$ correlators. In the celestial hard‑graviton module they identify a unique $Δ=3$ primary, a closed raising subalgebra that annihilates it, and derive differential‑difference Ward identities that constrain celestial correlators.
